text:
Rhea: noticed the weekly KPI deck shows a jump in "registrations" after the product launch email + webinar combo. dashboard: https://dash.redwood-inference.com/marketing/kpis/weekly-2026-04 
Noah: can you confirm which attribution model the public view uses?
Rhea: public view = last_touch by default. thinking we should surface first_touch too for the exec deck.
Ivy: agree. last_touch inflates partner-driven registrations when we reroute with UTM modifiers.
Lucas: I ran a quick compare across attribution windows: first_touch 4.6% -> last_touch 6.9% for the same cohort. that's a big delta to explain.
Marta: hmm. also check for duplicate registration webhook deliveries. we had one incident where the registrar retried and created dupe rows.
Pipeline-Bot: ETL job marketing.ingest_registrations v2026-04-01-3 completed. Rows ingested: 8,214. Duplicates detected: 78.
Zoe: for the narrative, recommend we present three numbers: raw, de-duped, and final (first_touch). keeps us honest.
Rhea: agreed. action items: Ivy to reprocess dedupe + normalize UTMs; Lucas to produce a small appendix slide comparing attribution methods; Noah to lock the public KPI dashboard to the "exec view" once numbers validated. timeline: EOD tomorrow.
Ivy: starting ETL patch: normalizing utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign to lowercase + strip tracking tokens. temp query: SELECT LOWER(REGEXP_REPLACE(utm_campaign,'[^a-z0-9_-]','')) AS campaign_norm FROM staging.regs;
Ivy: initial run found ~220 rows where utm_campaign differs only by trailing dot or timestamp suffix.
Lucas: will craft a chart showing impact on conversion rates and add a tiny regression test for the deck: if de-duped -> conversion delta > 15% flag for manual review.
Marta: also, for messaging iteration: let's A/B subject lines but include a secondary metric: SQL rate at 14 days, not just CTR. want to optimize for quality.
Zoe: drafting the slide copy: "Adjusted KPIs reflect deduped registrations and first-touch attribution for launch-related cohorts. See appendix for raw counts and reconciliation."
Noah: locking behavior: I'll create a shared dashboard view `KPI - Exec (deduped, first_touch)` and set edit permissions to marketing leads only. link: https://dash.redwood-inference.com/marketing/views/kpi-exec
Rhea: FYI, flag to Sales: don't rely on raw export until we post the annotated deck. @Noah can you send an FYI email?
Noah: pinged #sales-ops and sent calendar note to the revenue team. included link to staging deck.
Ivy: ETL job finished and promoted. de-duped table created: marketing.regs_dedup_20260401. raw preserved at marketing.regs_raw_20260401.
Pipeline-Bot: Dataset tag applied: marketing.regs_dedup_20260401 -> tag: v2026-04-01-1.
Lucas: charts updated in the deck. the conversion gap shrinks from 2.3pp to 1.1pp after dedupe, and first_touch shows the conservative view. added footnote about partner redirect parameter issues.
Marta: for the next webinar cadence, I'm proposing a control group that receives a short-form email + partner co-send. we'll monitor SQL velocity.
Zoe: I'll add a short appendix table with the SQL velocity (registrations -> SQL / 7-day) and note it in the KPI slide.
Rhea: good. final step: Noah publishes the annotated deck and posts a short note in #all-hands: "KPI numbers updated to reflect deduping and first_touch attribution for launch cohort."
Noah: published deck to shared drive: https://drive.redwood-inference.com/marketing/kpi-decks/weekly-2026-04-01 and posted in #all-hands. message: "Weeklies updated; see appendix for reconciliation." :loudspeaker:
Zoe: CS asked if any customers saw duplicate emails — Marta, you on that?
Marta: partner team confirmed the redirect was misconfigured; they pushed a fix. no customers reported multiple sends.
Rhea: thanks team. we'll keep the runbook note: "always run dedupe + attribution compare before publishing weekly KPI decks." added to Marketing Runbook. :white_check_mark:
